coverage.reason: No loading, empty or error state is added or altered. first-run.tsx's error state exists already and its copy is unchanged; what the hunk changes is which failure can reach it, which the accessibility review covers under FE-08 and the code review under FE-08.
Offline is untouched: no network call is added, and the service worker and its caching are outside scope.

coverage.evidence: A light review: in scope are rail.tsx's one added attribute, use-media-query.ts's internals and two statements in first-run.tsx's handler. Nothing in the hunks writes a design value directly. rail.tsx's added line is aria-label={label}, which carries no colour, spacing, radius or size at all. The colours around it map to tokens — bg-emerald, bg-ochre, bg-rose, bg-slate — and are untouched, as is the one dimension in the file, the bar's 6px height. use-media-query.ts holds the single breakpoint as DESKTOP, (min-width: 1440px), which is the value tokens.md and tailwind.config.ts define, and the hunk did not change it.

A light review: in scope are rail.tsx's one added attribute, use-media-query.ts's internals and two statements in first-run.tsx's handler. Tokens still come from one place: the hunks add no palette, scale or token of their own. The breakpoint stays exported once from use-media-query.ts with a comment pointing at tailwind.config.ts as its source, so the responsive decision has one definition rather than a literal repeated per screen.

coverage.reason: No token is added or renamed, so no token name is in scope. The existing names in rail.tsx are already purposeful rather than visual — positive, warning, danger, neutral, not the colours they resolve to.

A light review: in scope are rail.tsx's one added attribute, use-media-query.ts's internals and two statements in first-run.tsx's handler. Rail's states are unchanged in number and now more complete in substance. It is presentational — no pressed, focused, disabled or loading state applies, since it takes no input — and its four tones were all already present. What the hunk adds is the name assistive technology announces, which was the one thing missing from every one of those states rather than from a new one.

A light review: in scope are rail.tsx's one added attribute, use-media-query.ts's internals and two statements in first-run.tsx's handler. The danger tone's meaning is untouched by the hunk: the fills map is unchanged, danger still resolves to bg-rose, and the added attribute is text. The addendum reserves danger for money going wrong and nothing else, and this change neither widens that nor introduces a second use — it adds no tone, and no caller's tone choice changes.

A light review: in scope are rail.tsx's one added attribute, use-media-query.ts's internals and two statements in first-run.tsx's handler. Colour is not the only carrier, and the hunk strengthens that. Rail's tone is a colour; the proportion is also text in aria-valuetext, and as of this change the thing being measured is named in aria-label. Someone who cannot tell ochre from rose now gets both the figure and what it belongs to, where before they got a figure of something unnamed.

A light review: in scope are rail.tsx's one added attribute, use-media-query.ts's internals and two statements in first-run.tsx's handler. Text scales with the person's setting, and the hunk adds no text with a size. aria-label is unstyled. No font size, line height or fixed text dimension appears anywhere in the three changed files.

Checked by computing it from the tokens rather than deferred for want of a browser, which is possible because contrast is arithmetic on the values and both themes declare theirs in apps/web/src/design/tokens.css. Rail's fill against its own track is a user interface component boundary, so WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.11 applies and the bar is 3:1. Computed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula for all four tones in both themes: light emerald #0f5c3c on track #ede7da 6.51:1, ochre #8c5c15 4.66:1, slate #3c4a5a 7.35:1, rose #9e2b2b 6.01:1; dark emerald #4ecb8b on track #1a2129 7.92:1, ochre #e5a93f 7.79:1, slate #8fa7c0 6.54:1, rose #f0736b 5.70:1. All eight pass, the worst being light ochre at 4.66:1, comfortably above 3:1 and above 4.5:1 as well. Nothing in this change alters a token or a fill, so these are the ratios before and after it.

summary: Pass. DES-13 computed from the tokens rather than deferred: all four Rail tones clear 3:1 against their track in both themes, worst 4.66:1. Nothing visual changed. No colour, token, spacing or size is touched by any hunk — the one added attribute is text. DES-07 is strengthened: the thing a coloured bar measures is now named, not just its percentage.
